analysis:
Examined StartCommand+Modes.swift head (runForeground lines 209-236, 353-354, 489) and StartCommand+Picker.swift base/patch (lines 85-96).

Modes: the Autopilot start inventory now comes from AutopilotStartInventory.load. It is gated on hasConsent and on !privateOnly (head 224), and it fetches the catalog via coordinatorURL. The inventory falls back to the prior filter, which requires a verified non-empty weightHash (head 229-231). autopilotPending (head 232) passes cached builds not yet hashed to ProviderLoopConfig (head 354). The comment at head 222-223 says the provider verifies these after registration. Pending builds must not be advertised or served before weight-hash verification (T-012, T-027, A-004). That check lives in ProviderLoop and AutopilotStartInventory, which were not supplied.

Scheduled windows: selection.noteAutopilotCachedBuilds (head 489) carries loop-reported hashes across windows. Their validation source is also unseen. The catalog is coordinator-supplied, and the coordinator is trusted.

Picker: pickerLoadBudgetGiB and modelFitsBudget now delegate to AutopilotBuildEligibility (patch lines 88, 92). That implementation is not supplied. The earlier guards must remain: memoryGb finite, >0 and <=4096; sizeGb finite and >0. Their removal would be an availability/OOM issue only, not a confidentiality one.

No prompt, crypto, attestation, token or local-endpoint auth paths changed. The local-endpoint token handling is unchanged and still fails closed (head 325-335).

Integration must verify three things:
(1) AutopilotStartInventory.pending and inventory never let an unhashed or mismatched build into advertised models or modelHashes.
(2) The post-registration verification uses VerifiedWeightHashStore and catalog hashes and fails closed.
(3) AutopilotBuildEligibility preserves the finite/range guards.
